source_support_explanation: Vendor sequencer manual is not a general sequencing requirement; timing and fault behavior are application-defined.

current_topic_pack_statement: Sequence는 명령 출력만으로 단계완료를 판단하지 않고 위치·압력·속도·접점 등 독립적인 설비 피드백과 Timeout을 사용하여 성공, 지연, 고착, 센서불일치를 구분한다.
current_registry_statement: A Rockwell process sequencer separates commanded outputs from configured input feedback: the inputs monitor device or logic signals and determine whether the desired state or combination of states has been achieved to end a step. Its step-fault timer can flag when step completion exceeds the configured time. This supports feedback-qualified completion and timeout detection; distinguishing a mechanical jam from a failed or disagreeing sensor requires additional application-specific diagnostics and is not guaranteed by the sequencer inputs and timer alone.
source_support_explanation: Feedback and timeout choices vary by equipment and hazard; vendor implementation does not prove universal rule.

current_registry_statement: For a finite-dimensional LTI plant with observer-based state feedback, the nominal closed-loop characteristic polynomial factors into the state-feedback and observer-error factors, so their gains can be designed separately. Arbitrary pole assignment requires controllability of (A,B) and observability of (A,C); asymptotic stabilization requires (A,B) stabilizable and (A,C) detectable. Detectability alone does not guarantee that a stabilizing state-feedback gain exists.
source_support_explanation: Finite-dimensional LTI assumptions apply; stabilizability/detectability do not imply arbitrary pole assignment.

current_registry_statement: For a feasible continuous-time tracking problem, augmenting the controller with the integral of constant-reference output error supplies an integrator internal model. If the augmented closed loop is asymptotically stable, the plant has no blocking invariant zero at the origin for the selected input-output channel, and the actuator does not remain saturated, the error to a constant reference can converge to zero. Constant-disturbance rejection likewise depends on disturbance injection location and closed-loop feasibility; it is not unconditional.
